title: When THE PLANNER meets THE DRIFTER:
subtitle: The Myth of the Objective

script.text: In a vast, shimmering room that stretches infinitely in all directions—the Search Space—two explorers stand at the entrance.

One is THE PLANNER (representing Objective-Based Pursuit). He wears a suit and carries a GPS locked onto a specific coordinate: "Success." He believes the best way to get anywhere is to know exactly where you are going.

script.speaker: THE Planner
script.text: I have a plan

script.speaker: THE Planner
script.text: I have milestones. I have benchmarks. I have a grant proposal that defines my hypothesis. I will walk in a straight line toward the prize. Hard work and dedication will pay off

The other explorer is THE DRIFTER (representing Non-Objective Pursuit/Novelty Search). She wears comfortable shoes and carries nothing but curiosity. She believes the best way to find something great is to stop looking for it.

script.speaker: THE Drifter
script.text: You are walking into a trap

script.speaker: THE Drifter
script.text: The stepping stones to greatness do not look like the destination. You want to build a computer? You need vacuum tubes. But vacuum tubes were invented for radios, not computers. If you only look for computers, you will never invent the tube
The Planner scoffs.

script.speaker: THE PLANNER
script.text: That is inefficient. I optimize. I follow the gradient. Like the child's game: Hotter, Colder. If I am getting closer to the goal, I keep going

script.speaker: THE Drifter
script.text: But what if the goal is on the other side of a valley

script.speaker: THE Drifter
script.text: To get higher, you must first go lower. Your gradient will trap you on a local peak. You will be stuck improving the candle when you should be inventing the lightbulb
She points to the chaotic landscape of the Search Space.

script.speaker: THE CHAOTIC
script.text: Look at Elvis
, she says.

script.speaker: THE PLANNER
script.text: He was a truck driver who "acted the fool" in a studio. He didn't plan to invent Rock and Roll. Look at Microwave Ovens. They were found by a radar engineer with a melted chocolate bar. The greatest discoveries are not objectives; they are accidents

script.speaker: THE Planner
script.text: So we should just wander aimlessly

script.speaker: THE PLANNER
script.text: Not aimlessly
, corrects The Drifter.

script.speaker: THE DRIFTER
script.text: We should wander interestingly. We should collect stepping stones because they are novel, not because they lead somewhere. We should be like the treasure hunter who stops counting photographs in the newspaper because he sees the message: Stop counting. We should be open
The Planner looks at his GPS. It points straight ahead, into a fog.

script.speaker: THE Drifter
script.text: The objective is a security blanket

script.speaker: THE Drifter
script.text: It comforts you against the unpredictability of life. But it is a false comfort. It is a straitjacket. To achieve greatness, you must let go of the objective. You must trust the path
She turns and walks into the fog, following a trail of interesting rocks. The Planner hesitates, then takes a step off the path.

script.speaker: THE FOG
script.text: The future
, he realizes,

script.speaker: THE DRIFTER
script.text: is not a destination. It is a discovery
